key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 initially suppresses ETL/perovskite interfacial recombination, but thermal stress causes degradation to spread from the interface into the perovskite bulk.
engineering_relevance: This provides a nondestructive, depth-sensitive diagnostic for distinguishing interfacial versus bulk failure modes in perovskite solar cells during aging.
method: Compare wavelength-dependent PL decay to probe depth-dependent recombination
Use diffusion-recombination simulations to interpret surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime changes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that wavelength-dependent PL signatures changed with thermal aging, showing faster degradation in PEABF4-treated stacks and simulation-consistent shifts from interfacial to bulk-dominated losses.
watch_item: PL interpretation depends on model assumptions and excitation-depth calibration, so wavelength-dependent trends should be validated against complementary structural or electrical measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
